attributes.description: Fires when a disk device on the project node is busy for nearly all of the evaluation window. Disk IO is the most commonly exhausted resource on smaller Supabase compute tiers, and its exhaustion cascades into slower queries, connections held longer, and pool exhaustion.
attributes.name: [Supabase OTel] Disk IO saturation

investigation_guide.blob:
## Disk IO Saturation

`node_disk_io_time_seconds_total` counts device busy time, so its per-second rate is effectively utilisation: 1.0 means the device was busy for the entire window. On burstable compute tiers this appears as an abrupt throttle once the IO allowance is spent.

### Triage Steps
1. Read the `Avg Queue Depth` column. Above 1 means requests are queueing behind the device, not merely keeping it busy.
2. Check per-operation service time to confirm the device is slow rather than just busy: `node_disk_read_time_seconds_total / node_disk_reads_completed_total` and the write equivalents.
3. Look for the cause on the database side. The usual candidates are a fallen buffer cache hit ratio (`pg_stat_database_blks_read_total` rising against `pg_stat_database_blks_hit_total`), temp file spill from insufficient `work_mem`, and requested checkpoints outpacing timed ones.
4. Expect downstream alerts. Throttled IO means queries hold connections longer, so pool queueing and connection saturation follow from here rather than being separate incidents.

### Tuning
Matches the `Disk IO Time vs Disk Discard Time` dashboard panel aggregation. Rates can round marginally outside [0, 1] so the value is clamped before being presented as a percentage. Lower the 90% threshold on burstable tiers where sustained high IO burns a credit balance you cannot see in these metrics.
